Recommended Highlights This Week

1. NDP 2026 Preview 2 – 1 August

2. MAMAMOO Live in Singapore – 31 July

3. F1 Exhibition Singapore (closes 2 August)

4. Bouillon Gavroche – Mandarin Gallery

5. Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong – newly opened

6. Sentosa GrillFest (runs into mid-August)

7. Symphony in the Gardens – 1 August

8. A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa

9. CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa

10. The Portals Experience

Overall Summary

This is the last week to catch the F1 Exhibition before it closes on the 2nd, so it's worth flagging early to any motorsport fans still deciding. National Day season keeps building too – Preview 2 lands at the National Stadium on the 1st, and with MAMAMOO playing the Indoor Stadium on the 31st, expect Kallang to be busy again over the weekend. On the dining side, Bouillon Gavroche has quietly become one of the easiest Orchard Road recommendations we have – approachable French classics at very fair prices – and Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong has just opened its doors, giving us a fresh option for guests exploring the western side of the island.

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

The Line remains one of Singapore's most storied hotel buffets, prized for its spacious, light-filled dining room and its tradition of rotating regional showcases drawn from Shangri-La's sister properties across Southeast Asia – a format that has quietly made it a fixture of the city's hotel dining scene for decades. This month, the kitchen team turns the spotlight on Penang, Malaysia's street food capital, recreating its signature hawker dishes with hotel-buffet polish: fragrant char kway teow off the wok, a properly sour-spicy assam laksa, and other Penang classics reimagined across the spread. It's a theme that rewards guests who already love Malaysian food, and a good introduction for those who don't yet know why Penang's food culture has such a following.

  • Flavours of Penang Dinner Buffet – $98++ per adult, $49++ per child (6–11 years). Up to 30% off, Monday–Friday, exclusive to Shangri-La Circle members. Valid 13 July–5 August 2026.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

As Singapore's only beachfront resort, Rasa Sentosa leans into its setting with the Rasa Private Beach BBQ – a self-contained grilling experience set up right on the sand, away from the main restaurant crowds. Each package comes with its own grill, a curated spread of marinated seafood, meats and vegetables, and the option to add on beverage bundles, making it a good fit for small families or groups wanting a private, unhurried meal by the water.

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (serves 2 adults and 2 children). Available daily across three timeslots: 2:30pm–5:30pm, 5:30pm–8:30pm and 6:30pm–9:30pm. Valid 5 June–31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

J65 has built its reputation on generous seafood spreads and a halal-certified buffet that rotates through different themes across the week. The current International Dinner Buffet promotion sweetens an already-popular Sunday to Wednesday spread – Boston lobster, fresh seafood on ice, Black Angus beef rib and local favourites like laksa – with a straightforward group discount that works well for family dinners or small celebrations.

  • Dine 3, Pay 2 International Dinner Buffet – $88++ per adult, $44++ per child. Every group of 3 diners pays for only 2. Available Sunday–Wednesday, 6:00pm–9:30pm. Valid 21–31 July 2026.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

Makan@JEN sits right above Orchard Road, making it one of the more convenient buffet stops for guests already out shopping or sightseeing in the area. The restaurant offers both a la carte and buffet dining, with the buffet rotating between local, Asian and international themes through the week – a practical, no-fuss option for guests who want a solid meal without straying far from Orchard.

  • Daily lunch and dinner buffet – typically $30–55++ per person depending on the day's spread. 15% off the total bill for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Events & Festivals

Sentosa GrillFest

Sentosa's beachfront cookout continues, with 42 food vendors across five zones plus Chef's Grill, an eight-course omakase-style dinner served right on the sand.

Event Date: 23 July–16 August 2026 (selected Thu–Sun dates)

Time: 4:00pm–10:30pm

Location: Siloso Beach, Sentosa

Admission: Free entry; food and beverage purchased separately

Best For: Couples / Groups / Food Lovers / Sunset Diners

Concierge Recommendation: Still our strongest weekend recommendation. Tell guests to arrive for sunset, and to book Chef's Grill ahead if they want a seat – it continues to sell out on weekends.

F1 Exhibition Singapore

The motorsport exhibition wraps up its Singapore run this week, so this is the last call for guests who want to catch it before it closes.

Event Date: Closes 2 August 2026

Best For: Formula One Fans / Families / Repeat Visitors

Concierge Recommendation: Last chance this week – worth a direct mention to any guest who's been meaning to go but hasn't yet.

Attractions & Activities

A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa

Sentosa's Disney Cruise Line takeover continues across Palawan Beach, San Fransokyo Street, Toy Story Place and Marvel Landing. The Southernmost Point stays open till 10pm, lit up as a glowing coastal escape after dark.

Event Date: Until 20 September 2026

Location: Sentosa

Website: https://www.sentosa.com.sg/en/campaigns/magicalislandadventure/

Recommended Duration: Half day

Best For: Families / Disney Fans / Cruise Guests / Sentosa Visitors

Concierge Recommendation: Still one of our go-to family recommendations. If guests can stay into the evening, the Southernmost Point lighting is worth planning the visit around.

CRYBABY at Resorts World Sentosa

The five-metre inflatable sculptures – an anglerfish, a pufferfish and a whale shark – remain on display across RWS, alongside the CRYBABY pop-up store near the Coach Singapore boutique.

Event Date: Until 30 August 2026

Location: Resorts World Sentosa

Best For: Families / Young Adults / Collectors / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: Easy add-on for anyone already spending the day at RWS – free, quick, and great for photos.

The Portals Experience

A fantasy and sci-fi immersive experience built around original artworks, themed realms, miniatures and interactive displays – the kind of thing that photographs beautifully too.

Event Date: Until 2 September 2026

Time: 9:00am–9:00pm, last entry 8:00pm

Location: Fever Exhibition Hall, 25 Scotts Road

Admission: From S$26 for adults and S$17 for children

Website: https://portals-experience.sg/

Recommended Duration: 60–90 minutes

Best For: Families / Sci-Fi Fans / Fantasy Fans / Rainy Day / Orchard Area Guests

Concierge Recommendation: Handy one to have in your back pocket for guests based near Orchard, especially if it's raining or just too hot to be outside.

Restaurants & Bars

Bouillon Gavroche

Singapore's first traditional Parisian bouillon has settled into Mandarin Gallery, reviving 19th-century French comfort dining – hearty classics like Boeuf Bourguignon with Coquillettes and Oeufs Mimosa, served in a lively, unfussy dining room with red banquettes and vintage Parisian posters.

Location: 333A Orchard Road, #01-16/17, Mandarin Gallery, Singapore 238897

Opening Hours: Daily, 11:30am–10:30pm

Best For: Casual French Dining / Orchard Road Guests / Groups

Concierge Recommendation: A refreshing lower-key alternative to fine dining on Orchard Road. Good for a walk-in lunch between shopping stops – no reservation required.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Les Amis

Opened in 1994, Les Amis was Singapore's first independent fine-dining restaurant, and it remains one of the most quietly confident addresses in the city – a discreet glass frontage on Scotts Road that gives no hint of the three Michelin stars inside, or the roughly S$5 million wine cellar in the back. The kitchen is helmed by Chef Sebastien Lepinoy, who trained for 17 years under the late Joël Robuchon, and the cooking stays close to that lineage: classic French technique, occasionally nudged toward Japanese influence, built around ingredients rather than trends. Desserts are by Cheryl Koh, named Asia's Best Pastry Chef by the World's 50 Best in 2016.

Current Promotion: Les Amis Group runs an ongoing 15% off first-purchase e-voucher for new customers group-wide; no dish-specific promotion currently at Les Amis itself.

Operating Hours: Daily, 12:00pm–2:00pm (lunch) and 7:00pm–9:30pm (dinner)

Reservation Policy: Credit card details required to confirm – cancellations within 48 hours are non-refundable.

Address: 1 Scotts Road, #01-16 Shaw Centre, Singapore 228208

Website: https://www.lesamis.com.sg/

Signature Dish to Try: Cold angel hair pasta with kombu, caviar and black truffle – the dish most guests remember long after the meal, and a fair introduction to Lepinoy's whole approach.

Concierge Recommendation: This is a special-occasion recommendation – book well ahead, and mention the dress code (smart, with covered shoes and long trousers for gentlemen) when confirming.

Muthu's Curry

A Little India institution since 1969, when founder Muthu Ayyakkanu first started selling fish head curry from a small coffee shop on Klang Road. The restaurant – now run by his two sons – has grown into a proper Race Course Road landmark, but the format hasn't changed much: bold South Indian cooking, served on banana leaf, with tandoori chicken grilled to order in a clay oven right in the dining room.

Current Promotion: No specific promotion currently advertised – the restaurant runs occasional monthly specials, worth asking about on arrival.

Operating Hours: Daily, 10:30am–10:30pm

Reservation Policy: No credit card required – walk-ins welcome, though reservations are recommended for larger groups.

Address: 138 Race Course Road, #01-01, Singapore 218591

Website: https://www.muthuscurry.com/

Signature Dish to Try: Fish Head Curry ($32++, choice of sea bream, sea bass or red snapper) – a spicier, tamarind-forward take on the dish using a spice blend the family still keeps secret.

Concierge Recommendation: A great option for guests wanting an authentic (and communal) Little India meal – the fish head curry is meant for sharing, so suggest it for groups of three or more.

Concerts, Theatre & Entertainment

MAMAMOO Live in Singapore

MAMAMOO return to Singapore marking the girl group's 12th anniversary, with a setlist expected to include fan favourites like “HIP”, “EGOTISTIC” and “Starry Night”.

Event Date: 31 July 2026

Location: Singapore Indoor Stadium

Best For: K-pop Fans / Young Adults / Groups

Concierge Recommendation: Expect heavy crowds around the Indoor Stadium that evening, right in the middle of NDP Preview 2 preparations across Kallang – advise guests to build in extra travel time.

Symphony in the Gardens

The Singapore Symphony Orchestra's annual free outdoor concert returns to the Shaw Foundation Symphony Stage at the Singapore Botanic Gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, conducted by Nathanaël Iselin.

Event Date: 1 August 2026, 6:00pm

Location: Shaw Foundation Symphony Stage, Singapore Botanic Gardens

Admission: Free

Best For: Couples / Families / Classical Music Lovers / Picnic Guests

Concierge Recommendation: Encourage guests to bring a picnic mat and arrive early – lawn space fills up fast for this one, and it falls on the same evening as NDP Preview 2, so parts of town will be busy either way.

Hotel & Hospitality News

Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong

Resorts World Sentosa and Marriott International have opened Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong, following the refurbishment and rebranding of the former Genting Hotel Jurong. The 15-storey, 557-room property sits in the Jurong Lake District – Singapore's planned second CBD – within walking distance of Jurong East MRT and nearby malls including Jem, Westgate and IMM.

Address: Jurong Town Hall Road, Jurong Lake District, Singapore

Opened: 22 July 2026

Best For: Business Travellers / Extended Stays / West Singapore Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A useful new option to know for guests with business in the Jurong Lake District, or anyone splitting a stay between the city and the west side of the island.

Transport & Operational Updates

Downtown Line Night Works

Downtown Line trains stop earlier on Friday nights (last train around 11:30pm) and don’t start again until 8:30am on Saturday mornings. This continues until 5 September while engineering works are finished. Free shuttle buses run every 5–10 minutes between 5:00am and 8:30am on Saturday mornings to bridge the gap, connecting Bukit Panjang, Bugis, MacPherson and Expo stations.

PIE Overnight Closure – 2 August

Stretches of the PIE and adjoining roads near Potong Pasir/Bendemeer will close overnight from 12:00am to 5:00am on 2 August, for bridge-launching works on a new pedestrian and cycling link. Motorists on PIE heading toward Changi will be diverted via Exit 15 through Braddell Road and Upper Serangoon Road during this window. Unlikely to affect most guests, but worth knowing for anyone with a very early or overnight airport transfer that night.

NDP Preview 2 & MAMAMOO – Kallang Crowds

Kallang sees back-to-back events this weekend: on 31 July, MAMAMOO plays the Singapore Indoor Stadium, drawing concert-night traffic and crowds converging on the venue. The very next evening, 1 August, National Stadium hosts NDP Preview 2, with road closures around the stadium for rehearsal logistics, security screening and the fireworks display (approx. 7:30pm–8:30pm). With both events landing on consecutive nights in the same precinct, expect heavier and more prolonged congestion around Kallang than a single event would normally cause.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Airport traffic remains high with the mid-year travel season in full swing. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

SimplyGo Public Transport

Contactless Visa, Mastercard, Amex or NETS cards work directly on the MRT and buses – no separate transport card required.

Looking Ahead

National Day Preparations – Preview 2

NDP 2026 continues at the National Stadium in Kallang, with Preview 2 landing this week on 1 August, ahead of National Day itself on 9 August.

Event Date: Preview 2 – 1 August 2026

Location: National Stadium, Kallang

Fireworks Timing: Displays begin around 7:30pm, building to a finale around 8:10–8:30pm. Fired from Kallang Basin only – no Marina Bay fireworks this year.

Best Free Viewing Spots (no ticket needed):

  • Stadium Riverside Walk – closest unobstructed view of the Kallang Basin; gets crowded fast

  • Tanjong Rhu Promenade – quieter waterfront alternative across the basin

  • Kallang Riverside Park – open green space, good for guests with a picnic mat

  • Kallang Lawn Bowl – spacious grassy area, comfortable for families

Website: https://www.ndp.gov.sg

Concierge Recommendation: Expect diversions and crowds around Kallang/Stadium Boulevard on the 1st, compounded by MAMAMOO's concert the night before. If guests don't have a balloted ticket but still want to catch a glimpse, point them toward Stadium Riverside Walk – tell them to arrive by 6:45–7:00pm to secure a spot before the crowds build.

NDP 2026 Majulah Hunt

The island-wide digital treasure hunt continues – participants visit 61 landmarks (“Discoveries”) across Singapore and check in via an in-app camera, with a limited-edition National Day plushie up for grabs after seven Discoveries.

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, free way to get guests exploring beyond the usual tourist spots. Check-ins are capped at seven per week.

Upcoming Attractions & Events

Concierge colleagues should monitor announcements for the National Day Parade itself (9 August), and the continuation of Sentosa GrillFest through mid-August.

Concierge Recommendation: Useful for guests planning a return visit or extending their stay.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • This is the final week to catch the F1 Exhibition before it closes on the 2nd.

  • Expect heavy crowds around Kallang on 31 July and 1 August due to MAMAMOO and the NDP Preview – plan guest transport accordingly.

  • Weekend reservations are strongly recommended for ATLAS and other premium dining venues.

  • Bouillon Gavroche is walk-in only – no reservations, so advise guests to arrive outside peak lunch and dinner hours.

  • Symphony in the Gardens and NDP Preview 2 fall on the same weekend (1 August) – expect both Botanic Gardens and Kallang areas to be busier than usual.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day – Sentosa Family Escape

Morning: Take the Sentosa Express or cable car over – the cable car ride itself is worth it for the harbour views, and doubles as the first “attraction” of the day.

Midday: Work through A Magical Island Adventure's character meet-and-greets across Palawan Beach and San Fransokyo Street.

Afternoon: Stop for CRYBABY photos near the Coach boutique at RWS – quick, free, and on the way to the beach anyway.

Evening: Wind down at Sentosa GrillFest on Siloso Beach for sunset and dinner.

Tip: Suggest guests bring a change of shoes – Palawan Beach and Siloso Beach both involve sand, and the walk between zones is longer than it looks on the map.

Full Day – Civic District, Orchard & Dinner

Morning: Start at Merlion Park for the classic skyline photo, then walk through the Civic District past the Padang, City Hall and the old Supreme Court building (now National Gallery Singapore).

Midday: Explore the National Gallery itself, or continue on to Gardens by the Bay for the Supertrees and conservatories if guests prefer greenery over galleries.

Afternoon: Head to Orchard Road for shopping, then lunch or an early dinner at Bouillon Gavroche in Mandarin Gallery.

Evening: The Portals Experience on Scotts Road is a short walk from Mandarin Gallery and works well as an after-dinner stop; on 1 August specifically, swap this for Symphony in the Gardens at the Botanic Gardens instead.

Tip: This day covers two very different areas of town – Civic District and Orchard – so budget taxi or MRT time between the morning and afternoon halves rather than trying to walk it all.

2 Days – Marina Bay & Sentosa

Day 1 – Marina Bay & Chinatown

Morning: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark or the Helix Bridge for skyline views, then Gardens by the Bay.

Afternoon: Chinatown – the Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Chinatown Street Market, and a wander down Ann Siang Hill.

Evening: Dinner at Bouillon Gavroche, then a stroll along Marina Bay to see the skyline lit up.

Day 2 – Sentosa Island

Morning to Afternoon: Sentosa GrillFest prep, A Magical Island Adventure, CRYBABY photo stops.

Evening: Stay for GrillFest dinner on Siloso Beach as the day winds down.

Tip: Book Sentosa GrillFest's Chef's Grill ahead if guests want a seat – it's the one part of this two-day plan that can't be improvised on the day.

3 Days – The Full Singapore Sweep

Day 1: Orchard Road shopping and dining, capped with an evening at The Portals Experience or Bouillon Gavroche.

Day 2: Sentosa Island in full – GrillFest, Magical Island Adventure, CRYBABY – best done as a full day given how spread out the island is.

Day 3: Heritage morning through Kampong Glam (Sultan Mosque, Haji Lane) and Little India, followed by an evening built around whatever's on – NDP Preview 2 fireworks from Kallang Riverside Park on the 1st, or Symphony in the Gardens the same evening for a quieter alternative.

Tip: If NDP Preview 2 and Symphony in the Gardens both fall within the stay, let the guest choose based on energy level – one is a crowded public fireworks night, the other a relaxed picnic-on-the-lawn concert.

Quick Reference

Best Family Attraction: A Magical Island Adventure at Sentosa

Best Free Cultural Pick: Symphony in the Gardens

Best New Restaurant: Bouillon Gavroche

Best New Hotel: Four Points by Sheraton Singapore, Jurong

Best Concert: MAMAMOO Live in Singapore

Best Last-Chance Pick: F1 Exhibition Singapore (closes 2 August)

Best Weekend Recommendation: Sentosa GrillFest
